findings.title: Stale TODO comment and silent breaking change to MetricAlertDetectorHandler
findings.body: The TODO comment 'This will be a stateful detector when we build that abstraction' is now misleading: the class immediately below already extends StatefulDetectorHandler. More importantly, the previous implementation was a concrete class (it implemented `evaluate` returning `[]`) and could be instantiated as `MetricAlertDetectorHandler(detector)`. The new body is just `pass`, and because StatefulDetectorHandler adds new abstract methods (`get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, `counter_names`, `build_occurrence_and_event_data`), the class is now abstract. Any code path that resolves `Detector.detector_handler` for a `MetricAlertFire` detector — e.g., `Detector.detector_handler` calling `group_type.detector_handler(self)` — will now raise `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MetricAlertDetectorHandler` instead of returning a no-op handler. Even though the TODO claims the class 'won't be used yet', it is still wired up via `MetricAlertFire.detector_handler = MetricAlertDetectorHandler`, so the break is reachable. At minimum the stale TODO must be updated/removed; ideally the class should either remain concrete (with stub implementations of the new abstract methods) or the wiring in MetricAlertFire should be deferred.

findings.title: test_state_results_multi_group passes wrong value to build_mock_occurrence_and_event for group_2
findings.body: The data packet is built with `group_vals={'group_1': 6, 'group_2': 10}`, but the second call to `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` for `group_2` passes `6` as the value: `build_mock_occurrence_and_event(detector.detector_handler, 'group_2', 6, PriorityLevel.HIGH)`. The value for `group_2` should be `10` to match the data packet. The test still passes today only because `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` ignores its `value` argument entirely (it never uses it when constructing the IssueOccurrence). As soon as the mock builder starts using the value (for example, putting it into evidence_data or event_data), this test will silently assert against a stale/wrong occurrence and could mask a real bug. The hard-coded `6` should be changed to `10`.

findings.title: Behavior change to dict-keyed evaluate is not covered by tests
findings.body: The PR description explicitly motivates the signature change: 'return a dict keyed by groupkey instead of a list. This helps avoid the chance of duplicate results for the same group key.' The previous test `test_state_results_multi_group_dupe` (which fed `group_keys=['dupe', 'dupe']` and asserted the duplicate-handling error) was deleted. However, no replacement test was added that exercises the new deduplication contract: e.g., a test where `get_group_key_values` returns a dict containing the same group_key mapped to multiple values, or where two iterations of `evaluate_group_key_value` would yield the same `result.group_key`. Without such coverage, the stated motivation of the change is not regression-protected, and any future revert to a list (or a bug where `result.group_key != input group_key`) would not be caught.
